title: Check a stunned hull's route as her crew will sail it
message:
Check a stunned hull's route as her crew will sail it

The schedule route check sails a copy of the hull, stun included, and the
copy's stun never wears off, so it held her heading until the check gave
up: a Mind Blast hit on a scheduled hull at departure disabled her
schedule. The copy now sails with her crew fit, as with her rigging
whole.

title: Check a lock's target at every shot
message:
Check a lock's target at every shot

Only the gunnery tick dropped a lock on a contact that dived, entered
port, or left sight, so a shot before the next tick could still hit her.
vessel_locked_target() now drops such a lock wherever it is read: the
tick, shipfire, shipsight, and shiplock (review finding 3).

title: Refuse setsail to a stunned crew
message:
Refuse setsail to a stunned crew

The Mind Blast stun held the sail tick only, so a pilot could still
maneuver the hull one room, or climb and dive, with setsail while the
crew reeled. vessel_maneuver() now refuses them (review finding 2).

title: Keep a hull at her berth while the shipwrights work
message:
Keep a hull at her berth while the shipwrights work

Refits were accepted anywhere in port, so an owner could buy a weapon or
rearm while the crew was casting off, or after, and sail with the work
unfinished. The shipyard now takes work only from a berthed hull with no
departure under way (review finding 1).

title: Build a replacement merchant bow-on to her first leg
message:
Build a replacement merchant bow-on to her first leg

A new hull spawned facing north. At the Vailand north port, beach lies
one room east, so the route check sailed the fresh cog east through its
steerage turn onto the sand and refused the route: every replacement
Ironwind Trader failed to enter service. The merchant now spawns on the
bearing of the first waypoint off its spawn cell.

title: Share the open-water check and Duris speed scale; repair gate drift
message:
Share the open-water check and Duris speed scale; repair gate drift

vessel_open_water() and VESSEL_DURIS_SPEED_SCALE serve the hit model's
projection, the duel harness, the crash check, and the stun test instead
of three private copies and a literal.

The campaign provisioner re-enables its merchant's schedule when a
server disabled it on an earlier route revision: the development
database had the Vailand schedule off, which the provisioner's own
validation rejects. The frontier check matches the Survey Ship it
actually targets.

title: Gate S4 gunnery with an actual character
message:
Gate S4 gunnery with an actual character

Add --vessel-gunnery-check to the login helper and a --gunnery mode to
the tactical harness, wrapped by test_vessel_gunnery_in_game.sh: Kohdee
fits and sells a ballista and a ram at the east dock and meets the
shipyard's arc and capital refusals, is refused the harbor at battle
stations after locking a hull outside it, then scans, locks, sights, and
fires the starboard arc at sea.

The existing checks move to the S4 rules: shots wait out 20-second
reloads, a check that needs a hit fires until one lands (a natural 1
misses), coincident hulls lie off the fore arc, and the tactical and
damage checks volley from three shooters so the magazines and the clock
last; weapons show by slot in shipstatus.

title: Hold equal-warship duels to D2 under the S4 rules
message:
Hold equal-warship duels to D2 under the S4 rules

Study step S4 (decision D2, 3.3.4). The balance diagnostic's duel stops
simulating its own dice: two default warships with DurisMUD's frigate
combat fit (three large ballistae a beam and a heavy beamcannon) sail
and fight through the production sail tick, gunnery, damage, and reload
code, under a captain who brings the healthier beam to bear at about
7.5 rooms. The duels draw on the live random stream from a fixed seed
and restore it, so the report repeats. A duel without a kill in an hour
is a draw, allowed up to 2%: a smashed rudder cannot come about.

The verdict moves to D2: a 3-8 minute median, a 12 minute p95, nothing
under 90 s. Duris's 30 s and 45 s reloads gave a 9-minute median, so
the tuning lever the study names sets them to 20 s and 30 s: 200 duels
now give a 431 s median, 590 s p95, and 262 s minimum. The duels run on
the game loop, so the default drops to 200 and the most to 1,000.

greyhawk_getarc() becomes vessel_arc_toward() on hull pointers so the
harness hulls, which live outside the fleet array, get their arcs.
Help (SHIPFIRE reloads, VESSELDEBUG BALANCE) changes in both places; the
system, testing, and login guides describe the new sample.

title: Keep a crew at battle stations out of harbors and off the shoals
message:
Keep a crew at battle stations out of harbors and off the shoals

Study step S4 (3.3.2, L9). A hull at battle stations is refused port
rooms, so a hull under fire can no longer dash into harbor protection;
barred, she lies off the harbor with her orders kept until the crew
stands down, and setsail says why. She is also refused water shallower
than her class draft, the pre-S2 grounding test, so every seaport stays
open to hulls not fighting.

Any other refused room at battle stations, or with a crew stunned by a
mental blast, rolls DurisMUD's crash check: 2d50 against
(speed + 50) / (1 + 2 * sail mod) in Duris units, certain when stunned,
and a grounding lands hull weight / 25 + 1 hits of 1-9, the first on the
bow. This brings back the grounding S2 removed.

Help (SHIPFIRE, SPEED) changes in both places; VESSEL_SYSTEM.md replaces
its stale bathymetry grounding note.

title: Stun a crew with the Mind Blast Cannon
message:
Stun a crew with the Mind Blast Cannon

Study step S4 (3.3.4). A hit from the blast cannon does no damage: it
stuns the target's crew for 5 s at the cannon's reach rising to 20 s at
point blank. A stunned crew cannot steer, so the hull carries on as she
was, and cannot fire, reload, or repair. Inside mid-range everyone
aboard makes a Will save (DC 15) or falls prone for two rounds;
vessel_knockdown_aboard() now takes the save, Reflex for hull hits.

Help (SHIPFIRE) changes in both places; VESSEL_SYSTEM.md documents the
stun.

title: Aim naval gunnery by Duris geometry, locks, and arcs
message:
Aim naval gunnery by Duris geometry, locks, and arcs

Study step S4 (3.3.4, L6). A shot now hits on d20 + gunnery bonus
against a DC of 21 - round(20 * h), where h is DurisMUD's weaponsight()
chance for an untrained crew after its 2d50 roll: the range band, the
target's crossing speed, the swing of the bearing, and the closing speed
with both hulls projected a second ahead through the production sail
tick, target size from the class hull weight, and half again the miss
chance against a hull aloft. A stopped frigate is DC 1 at a quarter of
large-ballista range and DC 6 at its maximum. The bonus is the gunner
tier plus the firing character's Dexterity (Intelligence for lofted
weapons), at most +7; NPC crews fire at +5. Reloads shorten with the
gunner tier, criticals threaten by armor pierce.

shiplock puts the crew at battle stations, which hold 180 s after the
lock clears or the last shot fired or received; the lock drops when the
contact leaves sight, enters port, dives, or sinks. shipfire takes a slot
or an arc against the locked contact, naming a contact to lock it, and
refuses in port, at anchor, submerged, or sinking. shipsight shows each
weapon's DC and chance; shipscan reads a contact within 20 rooms (22
with a lookout); contacts shows the arc and the lock. Every vessel range
counts one room per 10 Z, gunnery uses exact positions, a hull aloft is
boarded only from within 10 Z, and submerged hulls are out of the fight.

Firing and NPC return fire move to the new src/vessels/vessels_gunnery.c.
Help (SHIPFIRE, CONTACTS, BOARD_HOSTILE) changes in both places with the
verifier; VESSEL_SYSTEM.md documents the model.

title: Fit weapons and equipment at the shipyard
message:
Fit weapons and equipment at the shipyard

Study step S4 (3.3.1, 3.3.4). Each class mounts what its DurisMUD analog
may, within the analog's mounts and weapon weight cap per arc, one
capital weapon, and its weight budget; vessel_fitout_problem() is the
one legality check, refusing both a purchase and a departure from a
berth.

The owner of a hull in port gets shipweapon (list, buy onto an arc,
sell for 90% or 10% damaged, swap slots), shipequip (one ram at 2 gold
per hull weight, free neutral colors that stay up while cargo is aboard)
and shiprearm (2 gold a round). A capital weapon needs a veteran gunner
until renown arrives in S7. Installation takes 75 s per weight point and
rearming 75 s per weapon; the shipwrights' runtime timer shows in
shipstatus and holds her in port, and immortals skip it. Unowned hulls
rearm whenever they berth, as they already re-rig.

Help (the crew and refits entry, UNDOCK) changes in both places with the
verifier's keyword and content counts; VESSEL_SYSTEM.md documents class
fitting, the shipyard, and maintenance.

title: Arm hulls from the Duris weapon catalogue
message:
Arm hulls from the Duris weapon catalogue

Study step S4 (3.3.4, 3.3.10). The twelve DurisMUD weapons and the ram
and neutral colors become static catalogue rows in the new
src/vessels/vessels_weapons.c, at 2 gold per platinum with reloads in
vessel ticks. A slot now names its catalogue row, arc, rounds left,
damage, and reload timer, so sixteen slots fit the 5 KiB struct budget;
the catalogue supplies range bands, damage, fragments, spread, sail hits,
and pierce, and beam cannons lose damage with range. Firing spends a
round and needs the target inside the weapon's band.

New hulls carry their class armament: large ballistae on a warship's bow
and beams, a medium ballista on the other armed classes' bow. Every slot
persists as a ship_weapons row with its catalogue row and ammunition
(Phase 20 SQL with rollback and verifier); a row saved before S4 loads as
the class default weapon on the same arc, fully loaded. The slot_data
snapshot, written beside those rows since both arrived, is retired with
its hex codec and the unused legacy weapon display helpers.

The class handling table gains the Duris hull weight, and fit-out weight
now comes from the catalogue. Help (SHIPFIRE, SHIPSTATUS) changes in
both places; VESSEL_SYSTEM.md gains a Weapons (S4) section.
